analysis: The 32→99 training-negative experiment completed successfully but reduced host macro validation HR@10 from 0.535 to 0.5025 (−0.0325). Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.500, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.530, Electronics 0.440, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.540. Macro HR@5 was 0.390 and HR@20 was 0.6488. This result does not support increasing negative coverage under the preserved training settings. More negatives change the sampled-softmax objective and subsequent sampler RNG consumption; the available evidence cannot isolate the cause of degradation. Training negatives remain sampled with replacement, unlike the evaluator’s unique negatives. Recorded GPU allocation was 1,478.23 seconds. No test metrics were available.
code_summary: Changed only NEGATIVES from 32 to 99, producing 100-candidate positive-first cross-entropy targets at each supervised position. Retained one independently trained SASRec per category: 64-dimensional tied item embeddings, learned item biases, positional embeddings, two causal single-head attention blocks, residual pointwise feed-forward layers, and dropout 0.5. Loss retains per-prefix normalized ten-transition half-life weighting, float32 scoring, and checkpointed chunks of 512 positions. AdamW, seed 42, supplied splits, runtime allocation, validation cadence, and strict HR@10 checkpoint selection remain unchanged. Prediction routes each category to exactly one selected checkpoint, with unchanged predictor generation and no ensemble or separately fitted scorer.
